$comment: THE actor manifest for Queen Euphoria. gen-actors.mjs holds no stat literals —
everything mechanical lives here, with a citation.
source: 'printed' entries carry a `page` (the printed folio, NOT the PDF page —
the offset is +2) and were read from a 300 dpi render. source: 'modeled' entries
were derived rather than transcribed and say what from. The validator checks only
'printed' entries against docs/CONVERSION-AUDIT.md.
_id is PINNED and permanent. Foundry's Adventure import matches on _id alone, so
a changed id is a DIFFERENT document — re-importing would duplicate while existing
tokens stayed bound to the old actor. Renaming an actor changes its display name
only. Never recycle a retired id.
art is explicit for the same reason: deriving it from the name means renaming an
actor silently un-wires its portrait.

retiredIds.e6c0660fae6813ab: Worker Ant Spirit (True Form, Force 3) — no such block is printed in the adventure. Retired, never reused. Nothing auto-deletes it from an existing world; see docs/UPGRADING.md.

$armorComment: Craft's Real Leather Clothing prints 0/2 (p.62) and Pride's prints 2/1 (p.26). Not a transcription error — kept as two entries so neither is quietly normalised to the other. Euphoria's Long Coat (4/2) is printed at p.63 and verified on the render — she wears it in public only; at home she has none.

$comment: sysName = method A: take the SR2 catalogue entry from
../sr2e-foundryvtt/packs-src/weapons by name, so no damage code is ever
hand-typed here. That is the whole point of method A and it removes the
single largest transcription risk in the module.
method 'B' = fold the SR1 staging digit into Power (p.283), used only where
no SR2 counterpart exists. `from` records the printed SR1 code so the
arithmetic stays checkable.

aresPredator.note: Craft p.62. Also stands in for the Ares Predator II (6M2) the Knight Errant guards carry — SR2 has no separate 'II'.

browningMaxPower.note: Lone Star p.14, Stone p.21. Also Pride's Browning Ultra-Power (6M2, p.26) — Ultra-Power is the SR1 name for this pistol.

hk227.note: Stands in for the H&K MP-5TX (p.19). Method A and method B agree here — B also gives 7M — so the choice is free.

stunBaton.note: Lone Star p.14, Strice Boys p.25. The printed '+ Special' is a stun effect beyond the damage code and stays a GM note.

concussionGrenade.note: Knight Errant p.19 carry two Airfoil IPE Concussion Grenades. These are why Throwing 3 matters; both were dropped together in the old actor.

spear.note: Pride p.26 Spear, +2 reach. Pole Arm is SR2's reach polearm entry.

lmg.note: The PRC-42D's nose gun (p.16). NOTE: methods disagree here — A gives 7S, B gives 8S. A wins on p.283's preference ordering. Re-check if the mislabelled Light_Machine_Gun_Generic file in the system pack resolves to a different weapon.

actors.name: Craft (Thomas Dorin)

spells.name: Sleep
spells.notes: His signature spell — how Euphoria is taken. The bonded Sleep Spell Focus (Force 2) adds 2 dice, but ONLY while the focus is active; see the focus item.

foci.name: Sleep Spell Focus
foci.notes: Printed at p.62 as 'Sleep Spell Focus (2)'. Bound to Sleep and left ACTIVE. It previously shipped inactive as a workaround: the system treated a focus as a permanent bonus on every spell, so an active focus handed Craft +2 on Mana Bolt too. sr2e 0.89.0 fixed that — a focus now serves only its bound spell, from a pool of 2 dice per action shared between the casting test and the Drain test, so leaving it on is both correct and what the page describes.

actors.bio:
Ant-totem shaman and the adventure's villain. A former Coyote shaman turned talismonger who runs the Magic Crafts shop; he took a run from his Fixer, Solomon Daniels, and came back changed. Under the Ant totem he is crazed with power, and his psychotic fixation on the simstar Euphoria drives the plot — he means to make her his Queen.

Totem: Ant. The book grants it no mechanical benefit; the bond is roleplay.

Sleep Spell Focus (Force 2) — a real item on this sheet, shipped inactive. Turn it on for Sleep and off again afterwards, or it adds its dice to every other spell he casts.

Cast of Characters, Queen Euphoria p.62. Attributes, skills and gear verified from a 300 dpi render; the spell list re-checked 2026-08-03 and confirmed at eight spells.

actors.name: Knight Errant Security Guard

actors.bio:
Knight Errant contract security. "Currently at a Group Three training level, these guards are a cut above the usual corporate security guard, but not elite."

Four are on Euphoria at all times: two precede her vehicle in a modified Ford Americar, one drives her Nightsky, one stays in the condo. These are the professionals slaughtered by Craft's Soldiers at the penthouse — their bodies are the horror the runners find.

For the PRC-42D Wasp pilot: use this block with Rotor 3 in place of Car 3 (QE p.16).

Queen Euphoria p.15 + p.19, both verified from renders. The old actor was wrong on six counts — Intelligence, Willpower, Essence, Unarmed Combat, three missing skills, an invented Stealth, and the wrong gun.

actors.name: Pacific Towers Security Guard

"Building security, barely trained and nearly inexperienced." The guards in the Pacific Towers lobby and on the residential floors.

Worth knowing: this block is attribute-identical to SR2's own Corporate Security Guard archetype (core p.205) — same eight attributes, same skills except SR2 adds Interrogation 2. The SR1 adventure and the SR2 core are printing the same archetype under two names.

Queen Euphoria p.15, verified from a render. The old actor was wrong on six counts: Charisma, Intelligence and Willpower all 3 instead of 2, an Armor Jacket instead of the printed Armor Vest, the wrong pistol, and no Etiquette.

actors.name: Lone Star Officer
actors.derivedFrom: Gear is printed at QE p.14. Attributes are NOT — the book says '(Use the Street Cop Contact, p.171 SR rules)', an SR1 archetype. actors.bio:
Lone Star officers. Four hold the Pacific Towers lobby (QE p.14), and more arrive if a Strice Matrix alert Traces the decker or a scene goes loud.

Attributes are not — the adventure defers to the SR1 Street Cop contact, so these come from SR2's own Corporate Security Guard archetype (core p.205), which happens to be identical to the Pacific Towers guard block on p.15.

The stun baton's printed "+ Special" is a stun effect beyond the damage code — GM adjudicates.

The old actor carried an Ares Predator and no baton or vest.

actors.bio:
Stone is a full magician, not a gunman — the module previously shipped him as a byte-identical copy of Osprey, with Magic 0, no spells and an Uzi. He has nine spells, Sorcery 7, Magic Theory 8 and a printed Magic Pool of 7.

Three bound elementals (separate actors in this compendium, and no link between them — the NPC data model has no boundSpirits field, so the assignment is recorded here rather than faked mechanically):

  • Fire Elemental Force 5 — assigned to Spell Defense.
  • Fire Elemental Force 4 — bound to him, for Combat Spells.
  • Earth Elemental Force 5.

Six expendable Manipulation fetishes. Armor, Control Thoughts and Petrify each need one to cast.

Queen Euphoria p.21, verified from a render.

actors.name: Pride (Shaka Jubowel)
actors.bio:
Shaka Jubowel, named for the great African conqueror Shaka Zulu, learned the magic of the Sixth World from shamans still carrying on ancient traditions before leaving to make a name for himself. As Pride he became a globally active shadowrunner specialising in bounty-hunting.

Almost two metres, muscular, very black skin, long stringy hair down the back of his neck, and eyes with vertical pupils like a cat's. He usually wears real leather clothing of African design. He behaves like an aristocrat, is always cunning, and becomes savage when angered. "Pride gives no quarter in combat."

Lion totem. Astral Pool 14. Sorcery specialises in Ritual sorcery — he is a ritual tracker, which is how a bounty hunter finds people.

Queen Euphoria p.26. This character had no actor at all. Block completed from the render 2026-08-03 — an earlier crop had lost Body, Armed Combat and three spells.

actors.name: Vincent Burroughs

Not a combatant: Defense pools of 1, no gear, no weapons. He is an interrogation and social encounter, not a fight.

If a Matrix Trace succeeds, the result prints at his terminal and he calls Lone Star — immediately if he is in-office by day, otherwise the next morning.

actors.name: Strice Foods Host
actors.derivedFrom: The printed SR1 system map at Queen Euphoria p.34. SR2E has no multi-node host, so the six printed nodes collapse to ONE host at a representative Security Code (Orange-4, the CPU tier). Each node's own colour-code drives MANUAL operation TNs the GM applies as the decker moves — recorded in the notes below. Each IC keeps its printed rating exactly.
actors.notes:
Strice Foods' deliberately low-cost corporate system (QE p.34), modelled as one SR2E host at Orange-4. The SR1 map's per-node codes are MANUAL:

  • SAN (gateway, #2206 / 312-1752) — Red-5, Access 5: a tougher Logon than the host baseline.
  • SPU-1 — Orange-3: Trace-and-Dump 3.
  • CPU — Orange-4: Barrier 3 + Tar Pit 4.
  • DS-1 — Orange-3, Barrier 4: purchase orders — the MegaMedia deal (1,280,000¥ for Euphoria's three appearances) and Knight Errant expenditures. 4 files × 70 Mp = 28,000¥ fenced.
  • DS-2 — Orange-5, Scramble 3: Accounts Receivable. 3 files × 80 Mp = 60,000¥.
  • DS-3 — Green-3: Seattle retailer/distributor list. 2 files × 40 Mp = 4,000¥.

Trigger: an external alert shuts the system down within two minutes. Any Trace result prints at Vincent Burroughs' terminal and he calls Lone Star — immediately if he is in-office by day, otherwise next morning. No vital clue lives here; the run is for paydata and the MegaMedia/Craft trail.

The ×3 vehicle-armour rule therefore does NOT apply here: the catalogue entry already prints SR2-scale armour, and doing both would double-count.

actors.name: Northrup PRC-42D Wasp
actors.derivedFrom: Method A for the chassis (../sr2e-foundryvtt/packs-src/vehicles/Northrup_PRC_42B_Wasp_b33a9832e56d2aaa.json) PLUS two printed deltas, because the D variant does NOT exist in SR2.
actors.$armorNote: THE ONE PLACE THE ×3 RULE STILL APPLIES. The PRC-42D is not in SR2, so its printed Armor 1 converts by core p.283 to Armor 3 — QE explicitly names the armour as Ares Armorflex. The other two vehicles take their catalogue armour instead, because method A supersedes there.
actors.notes:
Armed helicopter — a variant of the standard Wasp with Ares Armorflex vehicle armour.

Armament: one Light Machine Gun under the nose, 100 rounds (Belt, internal), Laser Sight, rigged for automatic 6 shots with no Recoil Modifier.

Pilot: QE p.16 says "use the Knight Errant Security Guard above, but substitute Rotor for Car at the same value" — so the p.19 block with Rotor 3. That is a note, not a separate actor.

Conversion: chassis by method A from the 42B; Armor 1 → 3 by the ×3 rule, which applies here and only here; the LMG by method A (7S). Method B would have given 8S — recorded in the audit as the one weapon where the two methods disagree.

actors.name: Juan Diablo
actors.$pageNote: QE p.10 does not print a block: "Use the Street Samurai stats for Diablo, page 46, SR rules, with Gunnery Skill 4." That is the 1st-edition archetype; this module converts to 2nd, so the stats below are the SR2E Street Samurai archetype (core p.62, read from a 300dpi render), plus the Gunnery 4 the adventure adds. Attributes are the AUGMENTED values the archetype prints in parentheses — Body 6 (8), Quickness 4 (5), Strength 6 (7), Reaction 5 (9) — matching how Osprey records his printed Reaction 5 (9) as 9.
actors.$essenceNote: The archetype prints Essence .1. Its own cyberware list does not reconcile: the six implants total 6.1 Essence at SR2E catalogue prices (5.9 without the Retractable Razors, which is exactly the printed .1). Recorded as printed rather than silently adjusting either the total or the list.

actors.bio:
A gang punk turned samurai on Ludivenko's money. Diablo is the razorguy at the first meet (Off and Running, p.8–10), riding escort for the Johnson's Toyota Elite. He backs up the Company Man if trouble breaks out, and otherwise stays quiet. If the runners turn violent, he and the chauffeur lay down cover while Mr. Johnson gets clear.

He is the runners' contact line. Diablo hands over his wristphone number so the team can reach their employers — which makes him the obvious thread to pull if they later want to work out who really hired them.

On his sheet: the Uzi III the adventure gives him, fitted with shock pads and a Smartgun Adapter to pair with his Smartlink; an armored vest with plates (4/3); his retractable razors at 7L; and the gun on the Harley — which is the whole reason the adventure bothers to give him Gunnery 4. The Harley's weapon is listed as an Ingram Valiant because the book never says what it is; swap it freely. The Ares Predator and stun baton come with the Street Samurai archetype QE points at.
actors.$artNote: Cropped from the Off and Running scene art — he is the razorguy on the Harley in it, so the portrait and the scene the players are shown are literally the same picture. Regenerate with `npm run handouts`.
actors.$poolNote: Combat Pool is derived by the system as (Q+I+W)/2 = (5+5+5)/2 = 7, which matches the archetype's printed Combat: 7. Nothing to store.
actors.$weaponNote: QE p.10 names only the Uzi III (shock pads + Smartgun Adapter) and 'the weaponry on his Harley'. The Ares Predator and Stun Baton come from the SR2E Street Samurai archetype the adventure tells you to use. The Harley gun is MODELED, not printed: the book never says what it is, so an Ingram Valiant stands in — swap it for anything you like, it exists so the Gunnery 4 has something to point at and so the sheet matches the bio.

actors.name: Mr. Johnson (Ludivenko)
actors.$pageNote: QE p.10: "Mr. Johnson, whose real name is unimportant, is an executive in Ludivenko's Seattle operations. (Use the Mr. Johnson Contact, p.170, SR rules.)" That is 1st edition; these are the SR2E Mr. Johnson contact stats (core p.210, read from a 300dpi render). The adventure separately states he has Negotiation Skill 6 — which is exactly what the SR2E contact already prints, confirming this is the right conversion target.
actors.$proNote: The contact prints Professional Rating 2-3; he is an executive, so 3.
actors.$essenceNote: Reconciles exactly: Datajack .2 + 200Mp headware memory 2.0 = 2.2, leaving 3.8.
actors.bio:
An executive in Ludivenko's Seattle operations — though he will not admit that, and the runners are not meant to find out at the meet. His real name does not matter.

The offer: 20,000¥ each to make Euphoria disappear before her first Amber Gel appearance. Negotiable — run an Opposed Negotiation Test against his Negotiation 6, and every net success moves the fee by 1,000¥ in the winner's favour. The payment plan is not negotiable: half after the abduction, half after Euphoria misses her last scheduled appearance.

The terms: take her from her penthouse the following night and hold her three days while the appearances come and go. He wants her kept at the rented Royal Meadows flat so he can watch both the star and the runners — "you, uhm, chummers can hold the lady anywhere you like, but your payments will be delivered to the rented flat." He will repeat that she must not be harmed: injured or dead, she is no use for Ludivenko's own ads.

Playing him: condescending, especially about questions he thinks are obvious. He answers anything reasonable. If the runners turn violent he runs for the car while the chauffeur and Juan Diablo cover him — and the deal collapses.

actors.name: Johnson's Bodyguard (Company Man)
actors.$pageNote: QE p.10: "The Toyota Elite's driver is Johnson's bodyguard. (Use the Company Man Contact, page 164, SR rules.)" 1st-edition pointer; these are the SR2E Company Man contact stats (core p.204, from a 300dpi render). The printed Vehicle skill is "Vehicle (Gamemaster's discretion for type): 5" — he drives the Elite, so it is recorded as Car 5.
actors.$essenceNote: Printed Essence 3, and like the Street Samurai archetype it does not quite reconcile: Wired Reflexes 1 (2.0) plus Skillwires 5 (0.5) is 2.5, which would leave 3.5. Recorded as printed.
actors.$reactionNote: Printed Reaction 4 (6); the (6) is Wired Reflexes 1, which also gives the second initiative die.

cyberware.name: Wired Reflexes
cyberware.notes: +2 Reaction, +1d6 Initiative — the (6) in the printed Reaction 4 (6).

gear.name: Silencer
gear.notes: Fitted to the Browning Max-Power (QE p.10).

gear.name: Explosive Ammo
gear.notes: Loaded in the Browning (QE p.10). +1 Power, Damage Level unchanged.

gear.name: Toyota Elite
gear.notes: He drives it. Mr. Johnson rides in the back.

actors.bio:
Chauffeur and bodyguard both. He drives the Toyota Elite that brings Mr. Johnson to Pier 36, and he opens the door. Corporate to the bone: he does the job, no questions asked.

He will not start anything. The adventure is explicit — he attacks only if the player characters become violent first. If they do, he and Juan Diablo lay down cover while Johnson gets to the car.

Loadout per QE: a lined coat (4/2) and a Browning Max-Power with a silencer and explosive ammo. With Firearms 7 and Wired Reflexes on a Reaction 6, he is a considerably harder proposition than he looks standing by the car.

$comment: QE prints SR1 spell names. Where SR2 renamed or merged a spell, map the
printed name to the system's canonical one so the sheet carries SR2's real
drain code and target rather than an SR1 approximation. Where SR2 has no
equivalent at all, `custom` keeps the spell rather than dropping it — the
spell equivalent of weapon method B.

Increase Strength.note: SR1 printed one spell per attribute ('Increase Strength +2: 4'); SR2 generalised them into a single Increase [Attribute] spell. Stone's is Strength +2 at Force 4 — recorded in the item notes since the generic spell carries no attribute field.

Treat Severe Wounds.note: SR1 printed a separate Treat spell per wound level; SR2 collapsed them into one Treat whose drain scales with the wound ((F/2)W). Force 5 as printed.

Detox Deadly Toxin.note: Same collapse as Treat — SR1's per-severity Detox variants became a single SR2 Detox. Force 5 as printed.

Petrify.note: NO SR2 EQUIVALENT EXISTS. Checked the core rulebook and Grimoire 2e: both have only 'Petrifying Gaze' as a critter power (basilisk, cockatrice), not a spell. Rather than drop one of Stone's three fetish-bound Manipulation spells — which would change the encounter — it is kept as a QE-local custom spell built on the SR1 printing and flagged as such on the item. This is the spell equivalent of weapon method B.
Petrify.$systemNote: Drain and target modelled on SR2's Control Thoughts — the nearest comparable Manipulation spell in power class (both are ((F/2)+2)D, limited range, resisted). Target is Body rather than Willpower since petrifaction acts on the body. GM should feel free to adjust; this is explicitly derived, not printed.
